title: A ROUTE TABLE -- how this host routes a task, on two axes, and which proofs it may run
description: ADR-022 decision 3. Routing is chosen on two facts a packet states -- how much unmade judgement it holds, and what a wrong answer costs to undo -- and the ANSWER in each cell is the host's: two teams route differently and both are right, so the kit ships the grammar and nothing in any cell. A cell may name the role it is routed to, the adapter, whether a verification profile is required, a budget ceiling and a packet ceiling. A profile is a NAMED argv run in the worker's tree on return -- the only thing the port will ever execute on a task's behalf. No cell declared is the declared zero: packets are carried and nothing is judged by their routing facts, which the port says.

role.description: The role a task in this cell is dispatched as.

adapter.description: The adapter a task in this cell is routed to.

ceiling_chars.description: The longest instruction a packet in this cell may carry: an inlined wall is re-billed on every call of the run.
